Draw only smooth white contour strokes with a thick uniform weight; all areas enclosed by outlines must be transparent empty space. No white-filled regions, textures, distress, stippling, speckles, shading or muscle hatching. Athletic adult man, blank oval head with NO facial features or hair, bare chest, plain shorts, bare feet. Smooth uninterrupted egg-shaped head, absolutely NO EARS or ear bumps, no eyes, nose, mouth, eyebrows or hair.

frames.pose: Full hold: the feet are off the floor and the toes pointed together behind the hips, the knees resting on the backs of the bent elbows. The elbows are bent at about 90 degrees angled out, the torso tilted forward, the back rounded and the head lifted looking forward.

Full hold: the body is horizontal and straight, supported on the hands with the elbows bent at about 90 degrees and set into the hips. Legs together and straight, extended behind, the feet are off the floor and the head is lifted looking forward with the torso level.

Push-up plank position facing right with the hands on the floor under the shoulders, the fingers pointing forward or slightly outward. Arms straight, the body in a straight line from head to heels, the feet together on the toes.

Full hold: the arms are locked straight, the shoulders far ahead of the hands, and the back is flat and horizontal. The hips are open so that the thighs are in line with the back, the knees bent at about 90 degrees with the shins pointing straight back, feet off the floor.

Full hold: the arms are locked straight and the shoulders are pushed forward past the hands. The knees are tucked tight to the chest with the hips bent, the back is rounded slightly, the hips level with the shoulders and the feet are off the floor.
Switch legs: near knee tucks under torso and far leg extends behind, maintaining forward shoulder lean.
Full straddle planche hold with straight arms and shoulders ahead of wrists.

Full hold: the body is one straight horizontal line from the head to the pointed toes, a hand-length above the floor, supported only on the hands. The arms are locked straight, the shoulders are protracted, the legs are together and straight and the hips are level.

Lowering midway: the body stays in the horizontal straight line as the elbows bend to about 90 degrees and tuck beside the ribs. The torso descends toward the floor and the shoulders stay forward of the hands.

Pulling up: the elbows bend and travel back as the chest rises toward the bar. The body stays a rigid straight plank from the heels to the shoulders, the heels dig into the floor and the head stays in line with the spine.

Mid rotation: the body inverted beneath the bar, the hips above the head level with the bar and the legs passing between the arms. The shoulders are rotating behind the body and the arms are straight, the back arching slightly as the legs pass over.

Lowering back: the arms stay straight as the tucked body rotates down behind the bar into a face-down position, hips and knees tucked in, the shoulders moving into extension. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Tuck Back Lever clearly in this side (facing left) view.

Full advanced tuck back lever: flat horizontal back, shoulders and hips level, torso facing the floor. Hips bent around 90 degrees with thighs descending below pelvis; knees bent around 90 degrees with shins extending behind. Straight arms extend behind the torso to the bar. Neutral neck and head.

Full hold: the torso is flat and horizontal with the arms straight and vertical. The hips are open so the thighs are in line with the back, the knees bent at 90 degrees with the shins pointing down. The knees are not tight to the chest, but the back stays flat, the shoulders pressed down.

Full hold: both feet off the floor, toes pointed and touching together behind the hips, shins resting on the backs of the upper arms. Arms straight or almost straight, back rounded and hips high, head lifted and looking ahead, shoulders forward of the wrists.

Full hold: the torso is flat and horizontal facing the floor, the arms straight beside the ears behind the bar. One leg is fully extended straight back in line with the torso, the other knee is tucked tight to the chest. The hips are level, the head neutral and the shoulders in extension.

Full hold: the torso flat and horizontal with the chest facing up, the arms straight and vertical to the bar. The knees tucked tight to the chest with the hips bent around 90 degrees and the thighs close to the torso, the head neutral, shoulders pushed down and the back flat.

Full hold: the torso is flat and horizontal with the chest facing up with the arms straight and vertical. One leg is fully extended straight back in line with the body, the other knee is tucked tight to the chest with the foot near the hip. The hips are level, the head neutral and the shoulders pressed down.

Full hold: the torso is flat and horizontal, facing the floor, the arms straight and held behind the body in line with the shoulders. Both legs are straight and spread wide in a straddle of about 60 to 90 degrees, toes pointed, hips level and the head neutral.

Full hold: the torso is flat and horizontal with the chest facing up, the arms straight and vertical to the bar. Both legs are straight and spread wide in a straddle, around 60 to 90 degrees apart, with toes pointed, the hips level with the shoulders, the head neutral.

Full hold: the whole body in one straight horizontal line, facing the floor, from the head to the pointed toes. The arms are straight and the legs together, the shoulders in extension, the hips level with the shoulders and the head neutral.
Full front lever: straight horizontal body with CHEST FACING UP, head right, feet left, two straight arms reaching up to bar. Hips and shoulders level, legs together.
Full one-arm front lever: rigid straight horizontal body, chest facing UP, head right, feet left; one straight arm reaches vertically up to bar, other arm held beside torso.

Chest-to-wall handstand in side profile facing RIGHT toward a wall at the far RIGHT. Hands are planted a full FOREARM LENGTH (about 35-45 cm) LEFT of the wall, leaving a clearly visible wide gap between wall and wrists. Arms locked straight, shoulders over wrists, torso tall with a gentle lean toward wall, legs straight together rising diagonally slightly right, only pointed toes touch wall. Chest and kneecaps face wall/right, toes point toward wall/right, heels left. Head neutral between shoulders, no chin turned backwards. Show ONLY a single vertical wall line well separated from body and hands; absolutely NO floor line, baseboard, corner, horizontal line or ground.

Bottom: the crown of the head just above or touching the floor, elbows deeply bent and flared, hips still stacked directly over the hands in the inverted V. Feet on the floor, legs nearly straight, torso almost vertical. Press arms fully straight to return to the top.

Full hold: the body in one vertical line stacked hands, shoulders, hips and pointed toes. Arms locked straight, shoulders open and pushed up by the ears, legs together and straight, gentle pressure through the fingertips, head neutral between the arms.

Landing the step: the right hand placed down about a hand-length ahead on the floor, both arms straight and shoulders open again. The legs return together into the vertical line, hips stacked over the hands, the body slightly advanced and toes pointed.

Bottom position of chest-to-wall handstand push-up in side profile facing RIGHT, wall on far RIGHT. Hands planted about a FOREARM LENGTH (35-45 cm) LEFT of wall, giving room for a tripod. Elbows bent 90 degrees, forearms near vertical, head lowered LEFT/in front of wrists to form wide stable tripod; crown near imaginary floor, face naturally toward wall/right. Torso upright, hips high, legs together straight leaning gently right to wall, toes touch wall. Clearly visible gap between wrists and wall at least one head width. Only one vertical wall line, absolutely no horizontal floor/ground line or baseboard.

Pressing up: the hips rise above the shoulders as the legs begin to extend upward behind the body. Arms stay straight and locked, the shoulders pushed forward over the hands, knees only partly straightened, toes pointing down toward the floor behind.

Bottom position: the elbows bent to 90 degrees and held tight in against the ribs, the upper arms parallel to the floor. The shoulders are lowered to the hands' level with the torso tilted forward and the legs raised overhead, the body in a straight diagonal line.
One-arm handstand with anatomically inverted head: chin points upward toward sternum, rounded crown points downward toward floor, neck enters upper edge of head.

Pressing up: the shoulders move forward over the wrists, arms locked, and the straight legs lift off the floor in a straddle, rising to horizontal. The hips are raised above the shoulders, the toes pointed and the legs wide apart.

Full hold: arms locked straight with the rings held beside the hips, palms facing in toward the body. The shoulders are pressed down away from the ears, the chest tall, the legs straight and together hanging with the feet off the floor, the head neutral.

Full hold: arms locked straight with the rings turned fully out, palms facing forward and the thumbs pointing out and away from the body. The rings are beside the hips, the chest tall, the shoulders pressed down, the legs together and the feet off the floor.

Adult athlete doing RING ROW top position, side profile. Feet at lower LEFT touching imaginary ground, body in one straight slanted line heels-hips-shoulders-head toward upper RIGHT. Chest faces UP toward ceiling, shoulder blades retracted. Elbows bent behind ribs, hands grasp two rings at chest height, straps vertically upward. Head in line with torso, face points diagonally UP AND LEFT in same direction as chest. Blank oval head, subtle chin at its UPPER LEFT edge toward sternum, nape at LOWER RIGHT continuous with upper back; cranium above-right of neck. No backwards chin on lower-right side, no ears, no face details. Two full arms, hands, legs. No floor line.

Gymnastics exercise demonstration: adult athlete on two gymnastics rings, at bottom of a dip repetition, both hands firmly grasp rings beside lower ribs, elbows bend 90 degrees behind torso. Chest faces right in three-quarter side view. Legs straight together pointing down; knees and feet fully visible. Two thin equipment straps rise directly from rings to top edge. Anatomically neutral head above shoulders. Plain sports shorts, blank oval head. Ordinary controlled gymnastics strength training.

Front view of band-assisted gymnastic iron cross. Athlete vertical, arms fully straight horizontally in a T, hands grip two rings at shoulder height. Two ring straps run vertically upward from rings. A resistance band is stretched from the left ring DOWN under BOTH FEET and UP to the right ring in a wide U/V; feet press securely onto bottom of band. Band stays BELOW the arms and torso. Head and neck entirely clear, with no straps behind or beside head. Legs together straight, toes downward. Single full body.

Gymnastics exercise demonstration: adult athlete at the completed upper support of ring muscle-up, shoulders above rings, elbows locked straight down, hands firmly grip rings alongside hips. Body upright, legs straight together down, toes pointed. Three-quarter side view facing right, full figure. Two thin equipment straps rise from the rings to top edge, clearly separated from body and head. Neutral head, plain sports shorts, blank oval head. Ordinary controlled gymnastics strength training.

Full hold: the arms are fully horizontal and straight, spread to both sides at shoulder height in a T shape, holding the rings. The body is vertical and straight between the rings, the legs together with the toes pointed, the head neutral and the chest tall.
Kip-up preparation with shoulders down, hips lifted, legs raised, elbows bent and two distinct natural palms planted beside ears, fingers toward shoulders.

Bridge reached: the feet land on the floor about shoulder width apart, the arms are straight and the hands remain on the floor. The hips are pushed up high, the back is fully arched, the head hangs between the arms and the knees are slightly bent.

Top position: arms locked straight in support above the bar, the bar at the hip level, the chest tall and the shoulders pressed down. The legs together and straight, slightly in front, the head neutral. The faceless head stays in line with the spine, and the limb angles of the Muscle-up must read clearly from the side (facing right) view.

Full hold: the body is horizontal and sideways from the pole, the bottom arm pushing straight and the top arm pulling, bent slightly. The knees are tucked tight to the chest, the hips are level with the hands, the head is turned toward the floor and the feet are off the floor.

Calisthenics HUMAN FLAG sports skill shown from front. A rigid vertical exercise pole at LEFT. Both hands grip pole with wide vertical separation: top hand overhead left and lower hand below left. BOTH elbows fully straight. Shoulder girdle between hands, torso extends horizontally RIGHT from pole, hips and locked straight legs continue in one horizontal line right, feet together pointed right. Body sideways supported by arms, perpendicular to pole. Full figure and pole contained with margins. Blank oval head naturally aligned with torso. Plain shorts.

Top support position of STRICT BAR MUSCLE-UP shown FRONT THREE-QUARTER view, adult chest faces viewer, head front neutral. One SINGLE long HORIZONTAL STRAIGHT BAR runs LEFT TO RIGHT across hips/upper thighs. BOTH hands clearly visible gripping SAME BAR at shoulder width, distinct left and right straight locked arms visible in front of torso sides, shoulders above hands. Both legs hang down together straight, torso vertical. This is a single pull-up bar, not two parallel bars: show BOTH bar ends extending past hands, no rails in depth, no dip-bar structure. No ground.

Adult gymnast at completed INVERTED MUSCLE-UP, in straight handstand over one horizontal bar, DIRECT FRONT view. Both hands firmly grip single bar at bottom, arms fully straight, shoulders-hips-toes stacked vertically. Show front chest, belly, FRONT THIGHS, KNEECAPS and TOPS OF FEET all facing viewer, never back of pelvis or buttocks. Legs together straight with pointed toes upward; soles face away from viewer, heel contours behind ankles; front kneecaps align with chest. Plain shorts front waistband and central fly, no buttock seams. Faceless smooth egg head neutral between arms. Anatomically continuous front orientation from torso through knees and feet.

Full hold: hanging by the right hand only, arm fully straight, the shoulder pulled down and engaged away from the ear, torso square to the front. The free left arm extends out to the side, legs together and straight, body vertical and still.

Top position: chin above the bar on the right side, the head and chest shifted over the right hand. Right elbow fully bent, left arm still straight and extended along the bar, hands still on the bar at original width, legs together straight down.

Bottom of the negative: working arm fully straight in a one-arm dead hang, shoulder packed down away from the ear, body hanging vertically and square. Free hand held out to the side, not touching the bar or the wrist. Legs together and straight.

Top position: chin clearly above the bar, the right elbow fully bent and tucked at the ribs, the right hand still the only contact with the bar. The free left arm is held out to the side, legs together and straight, body vertical with no kip.

Full hold: arms locked straight vertical, hands by the hips on the bars, shoulders pressed down and away from the ears, chest tall. Legs straight and together hanging in front of the body just forward of the vertical, feet off the floor, head neutral.

Bottom position: chest a fist's height off the floor, working right elbow bent past 90 degrees and tucked tight to the torso, body straight from head to heels and not twisted. Left hand still on the lower back, feet wide, head neutral looking down and slightly ahead.

Finish at the top after pressing back up: right arm fully extended and locked, shoulder just over the hand, body straight and square from head to heels. The left hand still rests on the lower back, feet wide, no hip twist or sag.

Full hold: the arms are locked straight and vertical, the shoulders pressed down, the hips lifted off the floor. The knees are tucked to the chest with the thighs near horizontal, the feet are off the floor, the back is upright and the head is neutral.

Full hold: the arms are locked straight, the shoulders pressed down, the hips lifted. Both legs are straight and spread wide in a straddle, lifted to horizontal level with the hips, toes pointed, the torso upright.

Top: the toes touch the bar, the legs straight and the hips piked to about 45 degrees, the torso leaning back and the arms straight. The back is rounded and the head is neutral, the toes at the level of the hands.

Full hold: the arms are locked straight, the shoulders pressed down. The legs are straight and raised above horizontal at about 45 degrees to the floor, forming a V with the torso, the torso leaning back, the hips lifted off the floor.

Perfect side profile of a gymnast performing FULL MANNA static hold on floor. Both palms planted with fingers pointing backwards left, straight arms vertical supporting shoulders. Shoulders at left and hips at right are at SAME HEIGHT, so torso is HORIZONTAL, chest faces UP. Hips pressed FORWARD beyond hands and high at shoulder height. Straight knees locked and legs tightly folded at hip; both legs extend HORIZONTALLY LEFT above chest and head, parallel to floor, toes pointed left. Draw a compressed sideways hairpin shape: horizontal torso below, horizontal straight legs above, connected at right-side hips. Neutral head at left end of torso, chin naturally toward chest. This is the advanced full Manna gymnastics pose with torso and legs both horizontal, not a V-sit. No equipment.

Full hold: the hips are lowered between the heels below the knees, the heels flat and the feet turned out. The chest is upright, the elbows are pressed inside the knees with the palms together in front of the chest, and the back is straight.

Full hold: the body hangs face down behind the rings with the arms straight and the shoulders in full extension behind the back. The back is arched, the hips are below the rings, the legs hang down and the head is neutral.

Rocking back: the hips shift back toward the heels and the hands turn so the fingers point back toward the knees. The palms stay flat and the arms stay straight, the wrists stretched in the opposite direction.

Full hold: the arms are straight and the legs nearly straight, the feet flat on the floor. The hips are pushed high with the back evenly arched, the head hangs between the arms, the shoulders open and the chest pushed over the hands.

Full hold: the right leg is straight in front with the toes pulled back, the left knee is bent under the hips. The torso is folded forward over the right leg with the chest toward the knee, the hands on the floor beside the leg, the hips square.

Full hold: the hips on the floor, the front right leg straight forward along the floor and the back left leg straight behind with the top of the foot down. The torso is upright and tall with the arms raised overhead and the hips square to the front.

Full hold: the legs are straight and spread wide, the knees and toes facing up. The torso is folded forward from the hips with the chest close to the floor, the arms extended forward along the floor and the back long.

Bridge reached: the hands are placed on the floor behind the feet, the arms straight and the legs nearly straight. The hips are pushed high and the back is fully arched, the head hangs between the arms. Reverse to stand again.

Top: the hips are fully extended and the body forms a straight line from the shoulders to the knees. The heels stay close to the hips with the knees bent, the arms flat on the floor and the head resting on the floor.

Bottom: the body is almost horizontal, still straight from the knees to the head, the chest nearly touching the floor. The hands are out in front of the chest, ready to catch the floor, the ankles anchored under the support.

Bottom of a DRAGON SQUAT: right supporting knee deeply bent, heel flat; left non-supporting leg crosses BEHIND and around the right supporting leg and extends straight diagonally to the RIGHT beyond it, hovering off floor. Clear crossed-leg configuration, not a pistol or shrimp squat. Torso leans slightly forward, arms reach forward for balance.

End: the forearm has rotated outward to about 90 degrees away from the stomach, pointing out to the side, the elbow still bent at 90 degrees and pinned against the towel at the ribs. The wrist is neutral, the shoulder is down and the torso upright.

Full hold: the front knee is touching the wall with the front heel flat on the floor, the shin angled far forward over the foot. The foot points straight at the wall, the knee tracks over the second toe, the back leg is straight and the torso upright.

Top: the arms are locked straight overhead with the bar above the crown of the head, the elbows fully extended. The shoulders are shrugged up slightly, the back is against the pad and the feet are flat on the floor.

Top: the bar is touching the lower chest or stomach, the elbows bent behind the torso and the shoulder blades squeezed together. The torso is hinged at about 45 degrees with the back flat, the knees slightly bent and the head neutral.

Top: the toes are lifted as high as possible toward the shins, the ankles fully flexed, with the heels still on the floor. The legs are straight and the back stays against the wall, the shins tight and the toes pointing up.

Full hold: the body is in a straight line from the head to the heels, supported on the forearms and toes, the elbows under the shoulders at 90 degrees. A weight plate rests flat on the lower back, the hips are level, the head neutral looking down.

Smash: at the top of the jump, the right arm extends and the racket strikes the shuttle overhead, the wrist snapping down. The body is rotated forward, the left arm drops to the chest and the feet are in the air.

Release: at the top of the jump the right arm extends fully and the wrist snaps forward, the ball leaving the fingertips toward the hoop. The left hand has dropped away, the legs are straight, the right hand is following through toward the rim.

Top: the climber has both hands matched on a large top hold above the head, the body extended up along the wall. The feet are on small holds, the knees bent and the hips close to the wall, the head tilted up to look at the hold.

Finish of the cross: the right arm is fully extended at shoulder height hitting the bag, the hips and shoulders rotated square. The back heel is lifted and pivoted, the left glove is back at the chin and the weight is on the front foot.

Submission: the athlete on the back has the legs and arms controlling the partner's arm in an armbar. One leg over the partner's chest, the other over the face, the hips raised and the partner's arm extended against the hips.

Follow-through: the bat swings down through the ball and finishes high over the left shoulder, the arms extended. The front foot has stepped forward with the knee bent, the weight is on the front leg and the head is over the ball.

Finish: the dancer is on the balls of the feet in a spin with both arms extended wide at shoulder height. The right leg is lifted with the knee bent and the toes pointed to the side, the torso is upright and the head is up.

Follow-through: the right leg has swung through to strike the ball with the laces and is now extended up in front. The ball is leaving the ground, the standing left leg is straight, the arms are out and the head is down.

Finish: the club has swung through the ball and ends high over the front shoulder. The hips and chest face the target, the weight is on the front foot with the back heel lifted, and the body is balanced upright.

Controlled hip throw in a judo lesson. Two adult partners in plain gi and belts. Thrower grips sleeve and lapel, turns back into partner, bends knees and lowers hips BELOW partner centre of gravity. Partner rotates over thrower hip, legs lift into air, thrower maintains grip for controlled descent. Distinct two bodies with natural joints, no impact or injury.

Finish: the right fist is fully extended at chest height in a straight punch, the wrist twisted palm down. The left fist is chambered at the left hip, the front knee is bent deeply and the back leg straight, the eyes forward.

Roundhouse contact: the right leg extends in a wide arc and the shin strikes a pad held at the waist height. The standing foot pivoted with the heel toward the target, the hips rotated, the torso leaning away and the guard up.

Finish: all students hold a front stance with the right arm extended in a straight punch at chest height. The left fists are chambered at the hips, the front knees are bent and the back legs are straight in a straight line.

Cow phase: the spine arches down, the chest lifts and the tailbone tilts up while the head lifts to look forward. The arms stay straight and the hands and knees stay in place. The faceless head stays in line with the spine, and the limb angles of the Mobility Flow must read clearly from the side (facing right) view.

The Hundred: the head and shoulders are lifted off the mat, the legs are extended at about 45 degrees to the floor. The arms are straight at the sides, pumping a few centimetres above the mat, and the abdominals are drawn in.

Release: the player's arms extend fully sideways and the ball is released from the hands toward a teammate on the left. The torso is rotated and the arms follow through, the legs in stride and the eyes on the receiver.
In the air: the skater and the board are above the ground with the board level under the feet. The knees are bent and drawn up, the arms are out wide for balance and the eyes are looking ahead.

Carving: the skis are fully on edge in a carved arc, the knees angled deeply into the turn and the torso facing down the slope. The outside ski is weighted, the poles are held out and the snow sprays from the ski edges.
Exit of the turn: the board flattens out and the snowboarder rises with the knees extending. The arms are out wide, the shoulders are parallel to the board and the snow sprays from the board's edge.

Next move: the right hand reaches high to the next hold and the left foot pushes up onto a higher foothold. The rope trails down to the harness, the hips rise and the body extends upward along the wall.

Follow-through: the racket swings forward and contacts the ball low and ahead of the body. The player lunges on the front leg with the knee bent, the racket arm extended along the wall and the eyes on the ball.

Full hold: the torso is folded forward over the straight legs with the head toward the shins, the hands resting on the floor or the shins. The knees are straight, the weight is over the balls of the feet and the hips are above the ankles.

Riding: the surfer stands on the board in a low crouch, the front knee bent over the front foot and the back leg bent over the tail. The arms are out for balance, the shoulders are turned toward the wave and the board rides across the wave face.

Follow-through: the paddle swings forward and up in front of the face after hitting the ball. The weight shifts onto the front foot, the hips and shoulders rotate toward the table and the right arm finishes bent near the left shoulder.

Follow-through: the racket has swung forward and up over the left shoulder after contact. The weight is on the front foot, the hips and shoulders rotated to face the net, the right arm wrapped across the body and the ball flying forward.

Higher: the climber is high on the wall holding two holds with the arms bent, the feet on footholds and the hips close to the wall. The rope runs straight up from the harness to the anchor above and down to a belayer at the base.

Landing: the right foot lands on a flat rock under the hips with the knee bent to absorb. The left leg is trailing behind with the heel up, the arms swing and the torso leans forward slightly with the eyes on the next footing.

Athlete on vertical Versaclimber machine, holding TWO distinct moving handles and standing on TWO foot pedals. RIGHT arm extended overhead with LEFT knee raised high; LEFT arm bent low with RIGHT leg extended low, opposite arm and leg pattern. Torso upright slightly forward, neutral head, all four contacts clearly visible.

Spike: at the top of the jump the right arm swings over and the open hand strikes the ball above the net, the arm extended. The body is rotated forward, the left arm drops to the chest and the feet are in the air.

Release: the right arm whips forward over the shoulder, the elbow extending and the ball leaving the hand toward the goal. The torso is high out of the water, the left arm pulls back and the eggbeater kick is still working below.

Rope passing under the feet: the athlete is in the air with the toes pointed and the feet a few centimetres above the floor. The rope passes beneath the feet, the elbows are tucked by the ribs, the wrists are turning and the vest rides on the torso.

Takedown finish: the attacking wrestler drives forward with the legs and lifts the opponent's legs off the mat. The opponent is tipped backward toward the mat, the attacker's head is tight to the ribs and the arms clasp behind the knees.

Warrior hold: the athlete has the front right knee bent at 90 degrees and the back left leg straight with the foot flat on the mat. The arms are extended overhead with the palms together, the torso is upright and the gaze is forward.
